title: Rani Durgavati
summary: After her husband Raja Dalpat died in 1548, she became regent of Gondwana for her young son Bir Narayan and ruled for 16 years. In 1564 the Mughal governor Asaf Khan invaded with a reported 50,000 troops. At Narhi her small force repulsed three imperial attacks over two days; wounded by two arrows, she took her own life rather than be captured. Historians dispute whether Gondwana was then fully annexed.

uncertainty.note: No birth date is given by the sources; this is the span of her regency.

as_recorded.value: invaded Gondwana with an army of 50,000 troops (1564)

where.modern_name: Singrampur, Damoh district, Madhya Pradesh, India (pinned to the village the Madhya Pradesh tourism board gives as the site of her last stand; Encyclopedia.com names the battle Narhi and her capital Chanragarh, which this pin does not locate)

importance.justification: Gond queen who resisted a Mughal invasion in 1564 and remains commemorated in India.

reviewer_note: Place is the least certain element: the tourism page says only that Singrampur marks the site of her last stand against Mughal forces and names no battle; Encyclopedia.com calls the battle Narhi and does not give coordinates. Treat the 40 km radius as covering this gap. Encyclopedia.com says Asaf Khan acted on his own initiative but with Akbar's permission. Army figures are as that page reports them.
